brief.t: Muthoot Finance gives loans against gold jewellery. It is the listed flagship of the Kerala-based Muthoot Group, whose gold loan business goes back to 1939.

Leadership changed on 1 October 2026: Alexander George became Managing Director, long-time MD George Alexander Muthoot became Executive Vice Chairman, and COO K.R. Bijimon was elevated to CEO. George Jacob Muthoot is Chairman.
FY 2025-26 was a record year: consolidated profit nearly doubled to ₹10,607 crore and loan AUM rose 49% to ₹1.82 lakh crore, helped by high gold prices.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026): consolidated profit ₹3,278 crore (+36%); loan AUM ₹2.09 lakh crore (+42%).

Watch point: Gross Stage 3 jumped to 3.87% in Sep 2026 as borrowers adjusted to RBI's new gold loan rules (monthly interest payments from April 2026), and a fall in gold prices in Nov 2026 hit gold lender shares.

model.how: Customers pledge gold jewellery and get a loan within minutes at a branch. Muthoot earns interest on these short loans. If a borrower does not repay, the company can auction the gold. Because loans are backed by gold, a rise in gold prices lets each gram support a bigger loan, and a fall shrinks the safety cushion.

Interest earned; gold returned on repayment
Unpaid loans: gold can be auctioned

points: RBI's revised gold loan rules (from April 2026) set loan-to-value limits by loan size and require regular interest servicing; this pushed up Muthoot's Stage 2 and Stage 3 loans in Q2 FY27.
Gold prices drive gold lenders: higher prices lift loan sizes and AUM, while a fall reduces the safety cushion on loans.
Gold loan NBFCs have asked RBI to ease capital rules (Tier-I capital and 100% risk weight on gold loans) to match banks.

glossary.NBFC: Non-Banking Financial Company: a lender regulated by the RBI that gives loans but cannot take savings or current account deposits like a bank.
glossary.AUM: Assets Under Management: the total loans an NBFC has given out and not yet been repaid. The main size measure for a lender.
glossary.Disbursements: New loans paid out to customers in a period.
glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The company's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on borrowings. A lender's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of loans or interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Loans not repaid for 90+ days (called 'Stage 3' loans by NBFCs), as a % of all loans.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.Stage 3 assets: Loans that have stopped paying for 90+ days. NBFCs report Gross and Net Stage 3, similar to banks' NPA.
glossary.Credit cost: Money set aside for bad loans, as a % of average loans. Lower means fewer losses.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The lender's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires NBFCs to keep at least 15%.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Borrowings: Money an NBFC raises from banks, bonds (NCDs), commercial paper and, for some, public deposits, to lend onward.
glossary.Cost of funds: The average interest an NBFC pays on its borrowings. NBFCs usually pay more than banks, so a strong credit rating matters.
glossary.Credit rating: An agency's grade (e.g. AAA) of how safely a company can repay debt. Higher ratings mean cheaper borrowing.
glossary.Upper Layer NBFC: The largest and most important NBFCs, named by the RBI under its scale-based rules. They face bank-like rules and must list on the stock market within 3 years.
glossary.Return on assets: Net profit as a % of average total assets. Shows how well a lender earns on what it owns.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates banks and NBFCs in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before giving a loan.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that lenders serve.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like insurance or a second loan) to an existing customer.
glossary.Co-lending: A bank and an NBFC lending together: the NBFC finds and services the borrower, the bank funds most of the loan.
glossary.IPO: Initial Public Offering: when a company first sells its shares to the public.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Gold loan: A loan given against gold jewellery kept as security. Quick to get; the gold is returned when the loan is repaid.
glossary.LTV: Loan-to-Value: the loan as a % of the value of the gold pledged. RBI caps it (up to 85% for small loans under the 2026 rules).
glossary.Stage 2 assets: Loans 31–90 days overdue: early warning signs before a loan turns bad (Stage 3).
glossary.Gold tonnage: The total weight of gold jewellery a lender holds as security. Shows real growth, separate from gold price moves.
glossary.Gold auction: When a borrower does not repay, the lender sells the pledged gold to recover the loan, after giving notice.

Finance.q: How do gold prices affect Muthoot's results?
Finance.a: Higher gold prices let each gram support a bigger loan, so AUM grows even when tonnage falls (204 vs 209 tonnes a year ago). A fall in prices cuts the LTV cushion and can hurt growth and asset quality.

Finance.q: Why did Gross Stage 3 jump to 3.87% in Q2 FY27?
Finance.a: Management linked it to borrowers adjusting to monthly interest payments under RBI's new rules from April 2026; Stage 2 also rose. Watch whether it comes back down.

Finance.q: Profit rose 36% but Stage 3 rose too. How do you read that?
Finance.a: Growth and margins are strong, but provisions jumped; the quality of the gold loan book now matters as much as growth.

Marketing.q: How would you attract first-time gold loan customers?
Marketing.a: Simple messaging on speed and safety of gold, regional-language campaigns, and doorstep or digital options linked to nearby branches.

Marketing.q: Banks also give gold loans. How does Muthoot stand out?
Marketing.a: Quick service, a large branch network, gold specialists at branches and a trusted brand built over decades.

HR.q: How would you help staff through a leadership change?
HR.a: Clear communication from the new MD and CEO, stable goals, training on the new RBI rules and recognition for branch teams.

Sales.q: Sell a gold loan to a small shop owner who needs stock money for Diwali.
Sales.a: Understand the need, explain the loan amount on their gold, the interest and monthly payment, stress safe custody and quick release, then close with a branch visit.

Operations.q: How would you reduce risk in gold loan branches?
Operations.a: Careful gold purity checks, strict LTV limits, secure vaults, tracking overdue accounts early and following RBI auction rules.

Other.q: What do you know about Muthoot Finance?
Other.a: A Kochi-based gold loan NBFC listed since 2011, led by MD Alexander George and Chairman George Jacob Muthoot; Q2 FY27 profit was ₹3,278 crore on loan AUM of ₹2.09 lakh crore.

gd.t: Are gold loans good for India's households?
gd.for: They give quick, low-paperwork credit using gold families already own.
gd.against: Borrowers can lose family jewellery if they cannot repay, and rising prices can encourage over-borrowing.

gd.t: Should RBI treat gold loan NBFCs the same as banks?
gd.for: Gold loans are secured and recover well, so rules should be equal.
gd.against: NBFCs lack deposit insurance and bank-level supervision, so stricter rules protect customers.
